Marathon Petroleum jumped 3.63% today as crude oil prices spiked above $105 per barrel following news that Saudi Arabia closed a major pipeline after a drone attack. Refinery utilization is running at 97.8%, near capacity, meaning the refiner benefits immediately when crude supplies tighten and prices rise — higher oil prices typically improve refinery margins (the profit spread between what they buy crude for and what they sell refined products for) when they're operating at full throttle like this.

The stock has climbed 10% over two weeks as Middle East tensions have escalated, pushing both U.S. and global oil prices sharply higher. With storage inventories at normal levels and refineries already maxed out, any supply disruption translates directly into stronger economics for refiners who can convert that more expensive crude into gasoline and diesel.
